title: First Example of Low-Valence Ion Substitution in Ln5O(OPri)13: Mixed-Valence Europium Oxoalkoxide [EuIII4EuIIO(OPri)12(HOPri)]·HOPri

synthesis.procedure: Syntheses were performed in a glovebox under dry, oxygen-free argon. Preferred metathesis–hydrolysis: EuI2·THFx was prepared from Eu metal and C2H4I2 in THF (Girard procedure) and desolvated in vacuum (ca. 5×10−2 Torr) at 140 °C for 4 h. Typically, 5.54 mmol (0.217 g) potassium was dissolved in 20 mL of 1:1 (v/v) toluene/HOPri, 0.39 mL of 1 M H2O in toluene/HOPri was added, then 1.58 mmol (0.409 g) EuCl3 and 3.97 mmol (0.161 g) EuI2 were added. After 48 h at room temperature the mixture was centrifuged; evaporation of the yellow solution gave dark yellow 1 (ca. 75% yield; yield increased by washing the salt precipitate three times with toluene/2-propanol). Alternative oxidation: [Eu4(OPri)10(HOPri)3]·2HOPri (0.148 mmol, 0.222 g) in 5 mL of 2:3 toluene/HOPri was treated with 0.0445 mmol (1.07 mL) dry O2 by gastight syringe; after 3 h vacuum evaporation gave dark yellow 1. Elongated rhombic crystals formed 1–2 days after adding toluene/HOPri to dissolve the initially obtained alkoxide powder.

properties.summary: UV–vis spectra of solid and dissolved 1 show a strong Eu2+ band from the UV to ca. 550–600 nm (orange-yellow color). Weak Eu3+ f–f features (5D1←7F0 and 5D0←7F0) are similar in solid and solution, supporting retention of the molecular structure in hexane or toluene/HOPri.
